item.title: [7] Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
item.description:
Last authors: Erez Berg, Netanel H. Lindner

Authors: Evgenii Zheltonozhskii, Barak A. Katzir, Yuval Oreg, Erez Berg, Netanel H. Lindner

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to topological quantum computing and FQH/superconductor experimental setups.

Tags: #quantumHall #superconductivity #topological

Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [G"ul et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $ u=1\pm rac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $ u=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $ u=1/3$ and $ u=2/5$. We propose comparing $ u=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

item.title: [8] Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS2: from disorder through 22 and 33 order to stripe order
item.description:
Last authors: Petar Pop\v{c}evi\'c, Victor Bal\'edent

Authors: Naveen Singh Dhami, Ricardo Guillermo Torres Ramirez, Gaurav Pransu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important structural phase diagram study of a van der Waals material with intercalation.

Tags: #vanderWaals #intercalation #structural

Abstract: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

item.title: [7] Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI2 (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
item.description:
Last authors: Charles Paillard, Laurent Bellaiche

Authors: Carmel Dansou, Charles Paillard, Laurent Bellaiche

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to VdW material electronic structure; compares Nb and Ta analogues.

Tags: #vanderWaals #electronicstructure #Peierls

Abstract: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $\eta$, and a Peierls mode $\delta$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

item.title: [8] Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
item.description:
Last authors: Haiqing Lin, Bing Huang

Authors: Zixuan Jia, Xuelei Sui, Shijie Hu, Tianxing Ma, Haiqing Lin, Bing Huang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance to bilayer nickelate superconductivity and spin-stripe physics.

Tags: #nickelate #Hubbard #superconductivity

Abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

item.title: [7] Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
item.description:
Last authors: Dinghui Wang, Tongshuai Zhu

Authors: Jiyang Fan, Dinghui Wang, Tongshuai Zhu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Useful interpretational tool for spin-polarized ARPES on AFM systems.

Tags: #photoemission #Floquet #antiferromagnet

Abstract: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

item.title: [7] The quantized Hall effect knows which way the current flows: mirror covariance and rectification in a laterally asymmetric Hall bar
item.description:
Last authors: A. Siddiki

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important transport study on quantum Hall effects with edge state relevance.

Tags: #transport #quantum-Hall #experiment

Abstract: The quantized Hall effect is the textbook emblem of universality: a resistance fixed by $h/e^2$, apparently indifferent to the shape of the sample, to its edges and to the direction of the current. That indifference is only half true. The plateau value is universal; the plateau is not. In a gate-defined Hall bar with one hard and one soft edge, reversing the current moves the plateau edge, and exchanging the edges reverses the move. We identify the symmetry that forces this. Because a perpendicular field breaks time reversal, the relevant operation is the in-plane $C_2$ rotation; within the self-consistent screening model it gives the covariance relation $R_\alpha[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(x),I]=R_\alpha[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(-x),-I]$, exact deep in the nonlinear regime and independent of linear response or microscopic reversibility. It predicts a rectification that is odd under exchange of the gate voltages and reverses with the magnetic field. The field-reversal test leaves the frozen lateral disorder untouched, so it holds for a single sample; it has not yet been performed. A further measurement, collapsing one incompressible strip, discriminates between co-directed and chiral pictures of the current. Self-consistent calculations show the soft-edge strip widening from 69 to 106\,nm on current reversal, moving the Hall resistance from 0.940 to $0.999994\,h/2e^2$ within a bounded window in magnetic field. The effect is a gate-tunable vector-product nonreciprocity, not magnetochiral anisotropy.

item.title: [7] Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
item.description:
Last authors: Pascal Simon, Ion Garate

Authors: Robin Durand, Pascal Simon, Ion Garate

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to topological materials and junction electrostatics in 2D systems.

Tags: #topological #Chern #theory

Abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and electrostatics in devices made from 2D materials.

item.title: [7] Field evolution of the multi-k magnetic states in NdB4 revealed by neutron diffraction
item.description:
Last authors: D. D. Khalyavin, O. A. Petrenko

Authors: D. Brunt, N. Qureshi, E. Chan, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering on a quantum magnet; relevant to magnetic topology/order.

Tags: #neutrons #magnetism #experiment

Abstract: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

item.title: [8] Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
item.description:
Last authors: N. G. Fytas, A. Berger

Authors: Z. Demir Vatansever, E. Vatansever, A. Vasilopoulos, N. G. Fytas, A. Berger

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Driving magnetic textures; highly relevant to magnetic topological materials.

Tags: #skyrmion #magnetic-topological #theory

Abstract: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

item.title: [7] Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS2 Transistors
item.description:
Last authors: D. Lin, K. De Greve

Authors: R. V. Upadya, M. Introna, X. Wu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Transport study on monolayer 2D material, relevant to user's broader interest in vdW heterostructures.

Tags: #material #transport #monolayer-MoS2

Abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.

item.title: [8] Longitudinal and Transverse Thermoelectric Properties in Topological Quantum Materials
item.description:
Last authors: Satya N. Guin, Koushik Pal

Authors: Jyoti Duhan, Anil Kumar B. M., Satya N. Guin, Koushik Pal

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Review of Dirac bands, Berry curvature, and topology in chalcogenides; highly relevant electronic structure focus.

Tags: #topic #topological #transport #Dirac

Abstract: Thermoelectric materials can be topologically trivial or non-trivial, enabling reversible interconversion of heat and electricity using a solid-state technology. Incidentally, few of the first experimentally discovered 3D topological materials, namely, Bi, Sb, Sn and Pb-based chalcogenides, were long known as good thermoelectric materials. In these compounds, the heavy atoms that give rise to strong spin-orbit coupling often become essential for band inversion and non-trivial band topology. They lead to low lattice thermal conductivity, linearly dispersing Dirac-like bands induce high electrical mobility, and a band-inverted electronic structure with multiple band extrema gives rise to high Seebeck coefficients. In materials, where the applied temperature gradient induces electrical voltage (Seebeck effect) in the same direction, they are termed as longitudinal thermoelectrics. On the other hand, when the generated electrical voltage and applied thermal current remain orthogonal to each other, the materials are termed as transverse thermoelectrics. The transverse response can be driven by an additional external magnetic field (ordinary Nernst effect), intrinsic remanent magnetisation, or non-zero Berry curvature of a material, which arises from their non-trivial topology (anomalous Nernst effect). We discuss another class of quantum materials, known as goniopolar materials, that exhibit axis-dependent conduction polarity and hence transverse thermoelectric effects, which are based on mechanisms of longitudinal thermoelectric properties. In this review, we cover both types of thermoelectricity, focusing on materials that possess non-trivial topological order. We make connections between their structures, topology and transport properties and suggest tunability of thermoelectric properties going beyond conventional mechanisms such as electron-phonon interactions.

item.title: [8] Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions (Sci. Adv.)
item.description:
Last authors: Fabian Hassler, Yoichi Ando

Authors: Jakob Schluck, Ella Nikodem, Anton Montag, et al.

Published as: Sci. Adv. DOI

Why: Experimental tunneling spectroscopy of topological surface state Andreev modes in Josephson junctions.

Abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). item.title: [8] Quantum Noise Spectroscopy of Criticality in an Atomically Thin Magnet
item.description:
Last authors: Shubhayu Chatterjee, Abhay N. Pasupathy

Authors: Mark E. Ziffer, Francisco Machado, Benedikt Ursprung, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental noise magnetometry study of critical dynamics in the 2D van der Waals magnet CrSBr.

Tags: #experiment #2D-magnet #vdW-material

Abstract: The universality class of a phase transition dictates the behavior of low-frequency and long-wavelength critical fluctuations in a material. Studying these dynamics in thin magnetic insulators, however, remains challenging; an experimental probe must be sensitive to low-frequency, long-wavelength fluctuations while navigating the sample's small volume, inherent inhomogeneities, and fabrication limitations. Using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, we demonstrate T$_2$ (spin-decoherence) noise magnetometry as a direct and quantitative probe of critical dynamics in a tri-layer sample of CrSBr, a two-dimensional van der Waals magnet. We observe a sharp increase in the decoherence rate of the NV spin ensemble at the sample's critical temperature, highlighting our probe's sensitivity to critical fluctuations. We demonstrate that the behavior of the NV spin decoherence rate below the critical temperature is inconsistent with fluctuations due to XY criticality in 2D CrSBr. Next, by simulating the NV spin decoherence dynamics using noise models for an Ising-type transition and fitting to our data, we quantitatively measure the dynamical and the correlation length critical exponents ($z$ and $\nu$) and demonstrate that the observed fluctuations strongly deviate from those predicted by the short-range Ising universality class. Together, these observations indicate that the transition is Ising-like but modified by long-range dipolar interactions, emphasizing the importance of easy-axis anisotropy and long-range interactions for understanding magnetism in 2D CrSBr. Our work establishes T$_2$ noise magnetometry as a quantitative probe of critical dynamics in 2D materials, opening a new avenue for studying strongly correlated phenomena at the atomically thin limit.

item.description:
Last authors: Shiv Kumar Ram, Amit Gupta

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of helicons as a probe of Berry curvature and topological charge in Weyl semimetals.

Tags: #theory #Weyl-semimetal #Berry-curvature

Abstract: Helicons are low-frequency, circularly polarized transverse electromagnetic modes that propagate in three-dimensional conducting systems in the presence of a static magnetic field. Here, we investigate helicon excitations in gapless multi-Weyl semimetals (mWSMs) with topological charge \(J=1,2,\) and \(3\) using semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory. We incorporate both Berry-curvature and orbital-magnetic-moment corrections into the quasiparticle dynamics and determine the optical-conductivity tensor in the presence of a weak static magnetic field. The longitudinal conductivity is obtained analytically for single-, double and triple-Weyl systems, whereas the transverse conductivity is evaluated numerically in the low-frequency regime relevant to helicon propagation. We find that the cyclotron frequency acquires a nontrivial dependence on the topological charge and on the magnetic field. The resulting helicon dispersion retains the characteristic quadratic dependence on the wave vector, while the axion-electrodynamics contribution generates an additional linear term. We further show that the axion term lifts the degeneracy of the gapped collective modes at zero wave vector, with the resulting mode frequencies determined by the \(J\)-dependent plasma frequencies. These results demonstrate that the helicon response provides a probe of the distinct electrodynamic properties of multi-Weyl semimetals.

item.description:
Last authors: Stefan Heinze, Dongzhe Li

Authors: Moritz A. Goerzen, Tim Drevelow, Soumyajyoti Haldar, Hendrik Schrautzer, Stefan Heinze, Dongzhe Li

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of magnetic solitons in specific Fe3GeTe2 van der Waals heterostructures.

Tags: #theory #vdW-magnet #solitons

Abstract: Soliton-based computing architectures have recently emerged as a promising avenue to overcome fundamental limitations of conventional information technologies, the von Neumann bottleneck. In this context, magnetic skyrmions have been widely considered for in-situ processing devices due to their mobility and enhanced lifetime in materials with broken inversion symmetry. However, modern applications in non-volatile reservoir or neuromorphic computing raise the additional demand for non-linear inter-soliton interactions. Here, we report that solitons in easy-plane magnets, such as bimerons and antibimerons, show greater versatility and potential for non-linear interactions than skyrmions and antiskyrmions, making them superior candidates for this class of applications. Using first-principles and transition state theory, we predict the coexistence of degenerate bimerons and antibimerons at zero field in a van der Waals heterostructure Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$/Cr$_2$Ge$_2$Te$_6$ -- an experimentally feasible system. We demonstrate that, owing to their distinct structural symmetry, bimerons exhibit fundamentally different behavior from skyrmions and cannot be regarded as their in-plane counterparts, as is often assumed. This distinction leads to unique properties of bimerons and antibimerons, which arise from the unbroken rotational symmetry in easy-plane magnets. These range from anisotropic soliton-soliton interactions to strong entropic effects on their lifetime, driven by the non-local nature of thermal excitations. Our findings reveal a broader richness of solitons in easy-plane magnets and underline their unique potential for spintronic devices.

item.description:
Last authors: F\'elix Casanova, Aur\'elien Manchon

Authors: Johann Coraux, Nicolas Rougemaille, Cedric Robert, et al.

Why: Broad critique and overview of the unique physics and challenges in 2D magnets.

Tags: #review #2D-magnet #vdW-material

Abstract: Magnetic two-dimensional (2D) crystals were isolated about a decade ago, triggering a tremendous research activity worldwide. This colloquium raises a stiff question: what is really new about them? At first sight, they seem to be purer implementations of 2D spin models than traditional systems such as ultra-thin films. Yet, they partly realized their promises so far, and whether they give fresh perspectives on long-standing predictions in statistical physics is still an open question. Undoubtedly, they are uniquely amenable to electric-field effect, susceptible to mechanical deformation, and sensitive to moir\'{e}s, for example. They represent interesting platforms for exploring, challenging, or simply revisiting a wide range of phenomena in condensed matter magnetism. This colloquium intends to offer a critical, yet not necessarily skeptical, overview of the field, clarifying what we believe could be unique with 2D magnets, related quasi-2D van der Waals magnets, and their heterostructures.

item.title: [8] Time Reversal Symmetry Breaking and Fragile Magnetic Superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Warren E. Pickett

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant discussion on TRSB and topological superconductivity in specific materials like LaNiGa2.

Tags: #TRSB #topologicalsuperconductivity #superconductivity

Abstract: Roughly twenty reports (as of 2025) of time-reversal-symmetry breaking (TRSB) states in low critical temperature (T$_c$) superconducting (SC), otherwise conventional Fermi liquid, metals have emerged primarily from muon spin relaxation ($\mu$SR) data. The detected fields, inferred from the current interpretation of depolarization data, are similar in magnitude and not far above the lower limit of detection, corresponding to magnetizations of no more than 10$^{-3}$ $\mu_B$/atom. These materials comprise a new class of {\it fragile magnetic superconductors} modeled as triplet pairing. The measured SC state properties, excepting only the fields detected below T$_c$, are representative of low T$_c$ singlet BCS SCs, not showing unusual coherence lengths or critical fields. While it is recognized that the muon does affect the sample by displacing nearby atoms and impacting magnetic interaction parameters, the measurement process, changing the system from sample $\rightarrow$ sample+$\mu^+$ thereby breaking TRS, may deserve further scrutiny. This overview provides a survey of the environment of the muon, from the normal state to the superfluid state, where the induced supercurrent and Yu-Shiba-Rusinov gap states provide coupling of the muon moment to the superfluid. The unusual topological superconductor LaNiGa$_2$, currently modeled as non-unitary triplet, is used as a case study. Supposing that the prevailing $\mu$SR inference of a small spontaneous field within the bulk of theSC obtains, the current picture of (possibly non-unitary) triplet pairing is discussed and an attractive alternative for LaNiGa$_2$ is noted.

item.description:
Last authors: K. D. Belashchenko

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important insights into altermagnets and interfacial spin-orbit effects highly relevant to topological/magnetic materials.

Tags: #altermagnet #spintronics #topologicalmaterials

Abstract: A surface antisymmetry group framework is developed to establish design rules for deterministic electrical switching of the N\'eel vector in a film of a collinear bipartite antiferromagnet. In centrosymmetric altermagnets, where linear current-induced spin-orbit torques vanish in the bulk, staggered effective fields can nevertheless exist as a macroscopic interfacial response, whose allowed tensor form is determined by the surface antisymmetry point group for the given surface orientation. Such effective fields do not require sublattice equivalence to be broken by the surface and can arise via the Edelstein mechanism driven by sublattice-odd interfacial spin-orbit coupling. General symmetry obstructions to bipolar switching that are valid to all orders in torque angular harmonics are also derived. Separately, the structure of the spin conductivity tensor determines which surface orientations allow transverse spin current generation via the nonrelativistic spin-splitter effect. Taken together, these symmetry-enforced properties establish which surface orientations of $d$-wave altermagnets can serve as deterministically switchable spin current sources in spin-torque heterostructures. Because the design rules are based solely on the surface antisymmetry point group, the symmetry-allowed staggered effective fields are robust against averaging over equilibrium surface roughness.

item.description:
Last authors: Maxim Dzero, Chandan Setty

Authors: Jaglul Hasan, Maxim Dzero, Chandan Setty

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant for understanding optical control and spin-orbit coupling in metals, applicable to ARPES studies.

Abstract: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) offers a promising route toward optical control of magnetic moments in quantum materials. Yet experiments on spin-orbit-coupled metals indicate that no single microscopic mechanism suffices, implicating orbital currents alongside spin polarization. We derive both responses in a disordered Rashba metal using quantum kinetics and diagrammatics with impurity-renormalized optical vertices, providing the first unified diagrammatic derivation of spin and orbital IFE. Treating impurity scattering consistently, our number-conserving kinetic formulation restores full phase-space derivatives and the optical magnetic field neglected in earlier treatments. We connect nonlinear orbital magnetization to absorptive linear optical conductivity, revealing that the magnetic Lorentz force supplies half the orbital response. Our unified treatment resolves both channels across the Rashba resonance: spin IFE changes sign as frequency increases, while the orbital IFE dominates, keeping the direction of the total magnetization unchanged.

Abstract: Vanadium Dioxide (VO2) and Vanadium Sesquioxide (V2O3) are Mott insulators that undergo an Insulator-to-Metal Transition (IMT) at ~340K and ~160K, respectively, manifested as an orders-of-magnitude reduction in their electrical resistance. Here, we show that the volatile switching in these materials can be strongly affected by non-volatile processes associated with the creation and annihilation of the conducting filament. These processes give rise to pronounced memory effects in which the initial switching voltage substantially exceeds that of subsequent cycles. We identify two distinct mechanisms underlying this behavior in different thermal regimes. In the phase-coexistence regime, a memory effect is observed in V2O3, arising from the spatial redistribution of metallic and insulating domains. Well below the hysteresis regime, an additional electroforming-like memory effect is observed in both VO2 and V2O3 which is attributed to the formation and/or migration of defects under the influence of a high electric field and a current surge associated with the IMT-driven switching. Using a protective internal resistor and a multi-step writing protocol, this normally destructive process can be harnessed to tune the switching voltage and power over a wide temperature range. These results demonstrate a route toward controlled programming of switching parameters in IMT-based resistive switching devices.

Abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moir\'e semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moir\'e materials.

Abstract: Many quantum phases, from topological orders to superfluids, are destabilized at finite temperature by the proliferation and motion of topological defects such as anyons or vortices. Conventional protection mechanisms rely on energetic gaps and fail once thermal fluctuations exceed the gap scale. Here we examine a complementary mechanism of entropic protection, in which defect nucleation is suppressed by coupling to mesoscopic auxiliary reservoirs of dimension $M$, generating an effective free-energy barrier that increases with temperature. In the Ising chain, this produces a characteristic three-regime evolution of the correlation length as a function of temperature - linear growth, entropy-controlled plateau, and eventual breakdown - indicating a general modification of defect behavior. Focusing on two spatial dimensions, where true finite-temperature topological order is forbidden in the thermodynamic limit, we show that entropic protection can nevertheless strongly enhance stabilization at finite system size, the regime directly relevant for quantum memory and experiments. Owing to the topological character of the defects, creation and transport are independently suppressed, yielding a double parametric reduction of logical errors in the entropic toric code and enhanced coherence when the framework is extended to Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Entropic barriers thus provide a passive and scalable route to stabilizing quantum phases in experimentally relevant regimes. We propose an experimental setup for entropic toric code using dual species Rydberg arrays with dressing.

item.title: [8] Quantum Magnonics: Quantum States Generation and Applications

Authors: Zi-Xu Lu, Xuan Zuo, Xin-Lei Hei, et al.

Why: Comprehensive review on quantum magnonics in real ferromagnetic materials, relevant to magnetism and quantum materials.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #review #magnonics #quantummaterials #ferromagnetism #superconductivity #phonons

Abstract: Hybrid systems based on magnons in ferromagnetic materials, such as yttrium iron garnet, have achieved remarkable development in the last decade. These include the coupling of magnons to microwave and optical photons, superconducting qubits, phonons, spins, the center-of-mass motion of a ferromagnet, etc. Here, we review both the experimental and theoretical progress in this field, focusing on the generation of magnonic quantum states and their applications in a broad range of fields. Since the strong coupling is a prerequisite for achieving coherent quantum control of magnons and preparing magnonic quantum states, we start by introducing representative strong-coupling experiments in cavity magnonics, then review a series of protocols for creating various magnonic quantum states, such as Fock, cat, squeezed, and entangled states, and discuss their potential applications in macroscopic quantum studies, quantum information science, quantum sensing, magnonic quantum devices, dark matter detection, and so on. Finally, we summarize the review and give an outlook for the future study of quantum magnonics.
